transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been worrying a lot more than I think is reasonable. I mean, everyone worries, especially in real estate, but lately it feels like it’s about everything—clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving into the condo was the right decision. It just seems a little out of proportion to what’s actually happening, if that makes sense.
Have you been worrying about a lot of different areas of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yes, I think so. It’s not just one thing, unfortunately. I wish it were that neat. It’s clients, the market, my family, money… even the condo move, which should be settled by now. I know some of that is normal to think about, but it feels like my mind keeps making everything bigger than it really is. Is that what you mean?
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yes… I mean, I can usually function, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. But it is hard to shut off sometimes. Even when I tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” one concern sort of leads into the next, and then I realize I’ve spent half an hour replaying little details I meant to let go. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Has this kind of excessive worrying been going on for at least six months?

Yes… I think so. It’s been more than six months. I’d say it really started after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo, so… about a year and maybe two months now. I don’t want to overstate it, but it has been around for quite a while.
Do you feel this worrying started because of the move into the condo?

Yes, I think it did start around then… or just after, really. After I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo, it seemed to kind of settle in. That was about a year and two months ago now. I don’t know if I should say the move “caused” it exactly, but the timing does line up.
Aside from the condo move, has there been any other major stressor in your life around the time this started?

Not that I can really think of. I mean, life always has little pressures, especially with work and family things here and there, but nothing major comes to mind around that time besides the move. I hope that’s a useful answer—I don’t want to miss something important.
Is most of your anxiety mainly about the condo move and its consequences?

Not just the condo, no… I mean, that’s definitely one of the things I keep circling back to—whether I made the right decision, what the consequences will be. But it’s broader than that. I find myself worrying about clients, the market, my family, money… honestly, kind of everything now. I know some of it sounds like normal life stuff, but it feels bigger than it should, if that makes sense.
Have you been having panic attacks?

I don’t think so… at least, not what I imagine a panic attack would be. I do get very worried and worked up sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed sudden attacks like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling restless or keyed up?

I’m not sure I’d call it restless exactly. I mean, I’m able to sit still and get through my day. There are times I feel a little wound up inside, but it’s not constant or anything… I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Do you have unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind over and over, even when you try to ignore them?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s more like worries that keep looping. Even when I tell myself, “Parin, this is not urgent,” one concern sort of leads into another, and then before I know it I’ve spent half an hour replaying small details I meant to just let go. Does that count as what you mean?
Do you do anything over and over, like checking, counting, or repeating things, to try to relieve these thoughts?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I might double-check something normal, like whether I locked the door, but not over and over to make a thought go away. I haven’t noticed counting or repeating things like that. Is that helpful?
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
Not really depressed, no. I mean, I have my off moments like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down in a serious way. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Has this worrying been interfering with your work or daily life?

A bit, yes… I don’t want to overstate it, because I’m still getting things done. But at work, even fairly straightforward listing negotiations or going through contracts are taking me longer than they used to. I’ll keep checking details because I don’t feel quite confident I’ve looked carefully enough, and then I end up delaying calls I should return sooner. Does that make sense?
Did this anxiety continue for more than six months after the move was over?

Yes… it did. I guess I kept thinking it would settle once the move was behind me, but it’s been about a year and two months now, since after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo. Not every minute or anything, but yes, longer than six months.
Do you feel your anxiety is much stronger than most people would have after a move like yours?

I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because the move was a big change, but it does feel stronger than what I’d expect. I came in because I seem to worry about everything now—clients, the market, my family, money, even whether moving to the condo was the right decision—and when I step back, it feels out of proportion to what’s actually happening. Does that answer it?
